findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. They are exposed in the repository, in Terraform state, and to any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration; the function should instead use its IAM execution role.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables holding secret material are protected only by the default AWS-managed Lambda key and are returned in cleartext to anyone able to describe the function. A customer-managed CMK with a restricted key policy would add a separate access-control boundary around the stored secrets.

The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS or the Node.js project, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound network access and no security group or NACL boundary. Combined with the embedded static credentials, this eases exfiltration if the function or a dependency is compromised.

The assume-role policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceArn or aws:SourceAccount condition, so the trust is not scoped to this specific function or account, weakening defence against confused-deputy abuse of the service principal.
